name: Glyph chain
source: A short title sequence in which ONE circle is carried through a whole chain of identities: the letter o in a word, a pupil, an eye, then the page the text lives on. Flat vector shapes on a pale ground, a dark inversion for the middle, and a small set of squash and morph moves. Described from a frame strip; no files or pixels are carried.

frame_device.what: There is no visible grid. The frame device is the carrier: one shape (a circle, here the letter o) that is always on screen and always the focus. A pale ground with a single flat silhouette or one small shape elsewhere; the carrier is the only thing that moves with intent.
frame_device.moves: The carrier travels along a path (arc, drop, rise) and changes identity at each stop (letter, dot, pupil, eye, page) with 0.3 to 0.6 s morphs, so each beat hands the next its object. The ground may invert (pale to dark) at the pivot beat for 0.3 s with the carrier unchanged.

type.classes: One neutral humanist or grotesque sans, regular to medium weight, sentence case; the hero line (3 to 5 words) at a readable large size, a small name or label at body size. Letters are ordinary glyphs: one of them is the carrier.
type.behaviour: Letters arrive one at a time (0.08 s stagger, tiny y offset) and sit fully readable at rest; the word is whole before the carrier leaves it. The carrier letter may lift out, but the word must read at once and again when it lands. No cropping, no hidden-letter puzzles.

image.treatment: Flat vector illustration only: a solid silhouette, a simple eye or mark built from circles, ellipses and one or two gradients at most. Product UI, when needed, is the last link in the chain: the carrier becomes a real UI element.
image.behaviour: Shapes do not slide in as pictures: they are built by the carrier morphing (a ring grows a pupil, a pupil lids into an eye) and stay in the same place, scaled.

transitions: carrier handoff (the carrier is the cut)
invert (ground flips pale to dark and back)
iris or pupil zoom into the next scene
scale up until the carrier is the page
morph to the next shape in place

techniques.name: Letter becomes the carrier
techniques.what: A letter o in the line separates from the word and becomes a free circle, the word closing up behind it.
techniques.route: Set the o as its own span; GSAP to the shape's position (0.5 s power3.inOut), a circle div (border-radius 50%) crossfades in under it 0.1 s before it leaves; neighbouring letters take its width with a stagger of 0.03 s.

techniques.name: Arc travel
techniques.what: The carrier moves along a curved path with its scale breathing, so travel reads as a toss, not a slide.
techniques.route: GSAP MotionPathPlugin (or two-axis tweens with different eases: x power1.inOut, y sine.inOut) over 0.7 s; scale 1 to 1.12 to 1 along the path.

techniques.name: Squash and settle
techniques.what: On landing the carrier squashes on the contact axis and rebounds with one overshoot.
techniques.route: scaleX 1 to 1.18 and scaleY 1 to 0.82 in 0.1 s power2.out, then elastic or back.out(2) to 1 over 0.35 s; shadow or ring optional.

techniques.name: Ring grow
techniques.what: The carrier gains a concentric ring (iris) around it, a second identity layered on the first.
techniques.route: An SVG circle with a stroke, or a second div, scaled 0 to 1 (0.4 s back.out(1.7)) behind the carrier; fill of the ring differs from the carrier.

techniques.name: Shape morph in place
techniques.what: A circle turns into a slit, an ellipse or a rounded rectangle without moving, each state a new meaning (round pupil, slit pupil, field).
techniques.route: Animate rx/ry on an SVG ellipse, or border-radius and scale on a div (0.4 s power2.inOut); for path morphs GSAP MorphSVG-style tween via paired path points authored with the same point count.

techniques.name: Lid and almond
techniques.what: A pair of curves (lids) close over and reopen the carrier, turning a dot into an eye with a blink.
techniques.route: Two SVG clip regions or a clipPath ellipse whose ry animates 1 to 0.05 to 1 (0.18 s in, 0.25 s out, power2); the carrier and a small highlight dot sit inside the clip.

techniques.name: Ground invert
techniques.what: The pale ground flips to dark at the pivot beat so the carrier's change of identity lands with contrast.
techniques.route: A full-frame div animates background colour (0.3 s) while the carrier's fill is unchanged; text colour swaps in sync; avoid blur and glow.

techniques.name: Scale until it is the page
techniques.what: The carrier (an eye's white, a ring) scales until its fill is the whole frame and becomes the next scene's background.
techniques.route: Scale the carrier's fill circle 1 to 20+ (0.7 s expo.in) with its colour matching the next ground; the next scene's content fades in 0.15 s before the scale completes.

techniques.name: Highlight dot
techniques.what: A small white dot sits on the carrier and moves with a lag, giving a flat circle life.
techniques.route: A child circle at 18% size, offset to one quadrant; offset it by -4 to 6 px against the carrier's motion with a 0.08 s lag (a second tween, same ease, delay 0.08).

techniques.name: Word out of the shape
techniques.what: The shape resolves into the final line: letters of the product's name are released from inside the carrier and read at once.
techniques.route: Text set under a clip-path circle matching the carrier; scale the clip-path out (0.6 s expo.out) while letters stagger y 12 to 0 (0.04 s); the carrier fades only after the last letter lands.

techniques.name: Iris cut
techniques.what: The carrier is a circular mask that opens (or closes) on the next scene, so the cut is the carrier.
techniques.route: clip-path circle(0 at X Y) to circle(150% at X Y) on the incoming scene (0.7 s expo.inOut), X and Y at the carrier's centre; the outgoing scene is left unchanged.

signature: One circle, many identities: the letter o becomes a pupil, an eye, then the page the line is written on.

density.note: The carrier changes identity roughly every 0.6 to 1 s; between changes only small settles. Holds are pauses of the camera, not of the carrier.

palette.ground: a pale cool grey (#EEF2F5) with a deep navy inversion (#0A0E1A)
palette.ink: near black for type and silhouettes
palette.accent: one warm amber or the brand's accent for the carrier
palette.note: A brand palette overrides these; the devices stay. The carrier is the brand's accent.

do: Choose ONE carrier shape and keep it on screen the whole film
Make every change of identity a morph or a handoff, never a cut
Give the carrier squash, overshoot and a lag on its highlight
Keep the line readable the whole time
Invert the ground once at the pivot, not repeatedly
End with the carrier as the product's real mark or UI element
dont: Do not use a second competing shape
Do not hide or crop letters so the line cannot be read
Do not add blur, glow, grain or 3D
Do not carry the shape through metaphors that never land on the product
Do not let the chain exceed what the viewer can follow: one change per 0.6 s at the fastest
fits: launch ladder (the carrier threads the rungs)
